subject.title: fix(xai): respect ssrfPolicy and request.allowPrivateNetwork in image_generate

question: Should xAI image generation treat the global browser SSRF opt-in as explicit authorization that overrides a provider-level `allowPrivateNetwork: false`, while also enabling the full sanitized xAI request policy on this path?
rationale: The patch is mechanically consistent with shared infrastructure, but it intentionally broadens a network security boundary and activates request controls beyond the narrowly reported failure; repository behavior cannot determine the desired authorization scope.

options.title: Approve after scoped proof
options.body: Confirm the shared precedence and full configured-request scope, require current-head provider-path proof, and retain the patch structure.

options.title: Limit to provider opt-in
options.body: Authorize private xAI image endpoints only through the provider request setting if the global browser policy should not govern this provider.

options.title: Keep the hard deny
options.body: Decline private-network xAI image generation if this provider should remain excluded from configurable SSRF authorization.

recommendation.title: Approve after scoped proof
recommendation.body: Confirm the shared precedence and full configured-request scope, require current-head provider-path proof, and retain the patch structure.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on image-provider private-network authorization and redirect boundaries makes this the strongest available routing signal for the security-scope choice.
